grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; none of Rules A–F imposes a cap. The statement that the terminal set S_p^* always has one element is only a harmless wording imprecision: when p does not divide M it is empty, and the explicitly declared empty-gcd convention gives g_p=v_p(M)=0.
grade.summary: The submission completely proves termination using the well-founded lexicographic behavior of the product P and the number C of entries greater than 1. It then proves that the gcd of the positive p-adic exponents is invariant under each move and reconstructs the unique terminal entry prime by prime, establishing independence of all choices.
strengths: Correctly distinguishes the coprime and non-coprime cases: P stays fixed while C decreases in the former, and P strictly decreases in the latter.
Correctly proves that at least one entry greater than 1 persists, so a terminal board has exactly one such entry.
Correctly identifies the transformation of p-adic exponents and proves invariance of their nonzero gcd, which uniquely determines every exponent of M.

errors.description: For primes p not dividing the terminal M, S_p^* is empty rather than a singleton containing v_p(M)=0. The submission's empty-set convention makes the ensuing equality correct, so this does not create a proof gap.
